title: Correctness at the Initial Time
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape alphabet, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $W\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $xb:\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose every local checker condition holds for every time $t<2^W$, address $a<2^W$, position $j\le |x|+1$, and checker. Also suppose $xb(j)=x_j$ for every $j<|x|$. Then at time zero the encoded state and output register agree with the machine's initial configuration; every encoded work-tape symbol at offset $d$ agrees with the initial work tape whenever $|d|\le 2^W-1$; and every encoded input symbol at offset $d$ agrees with the initial input tape whenever $|d|\le |x|+1$.
hypotheses_covered: All local checker conditions for $t<2^W$, $a<2^W$, $j\le |x|+1$, and every checker
